long_biography.plain_text:
Roman Abramovich reshaped his holdings in 2005 when he sold control of Sibneft to Gazprom. He had built an oil-products trading business and then acquired the producer during post-Soviet privatisation. The transaction converted an operating energy asset into capital for investments across other sectors.

Steelmaker Evraz and nickel producer Norilsk Nickel became major parts of the resulting portfolio. After Sibneft, his business interests centred increasingly on investment stakes rather than management of a single successor company. Together, they diversified the industrial base of his portfolio beyond the energy business that had created the original fortune.
